# Create a paid campaign

Write the ads the user asked for, and when the user wants a campaign, plan the smallest test that
can find a winner. Do not treat spend, reach, or clicks as the strategy.

## Write the ads

Write the ads in your own judgment from the user's facts. This covers every ad this command
drafts, alone or inside a campaign: Meta, Google, LinkedIn, TikTok, and Apple variations,
headlines, descriptions, and video scripts. Load no other file for it; the dated platform facts
are in `ENTRY.md`. Then run only the facts check: remove claims the facts do not
support, keep fair inferences, and add nothing (no hedges, no source text, no disclaimers). Return
the ads in the format the user asked for.

Ask at most one bundled question when a missing fact would change the ads materially. Otherwise
label the assumption and continue.

## Plan the test (campaign requests)

Choose one network, one audience, one offer, and one destination per test. Before cold paid traffic,
confirm three things: the product already converts from organic, creator, or sales traffic; the
conversion event fires and is tracked; and the landing page repeats the ad's promise and terms. If
one is missing, say so and propose the step that fixes it before spend.

Test concepts, not wording. Each concept is a different bet on why this reader buys, with its own
visual; platforms group ads that look and read alike, so a reworded ad is not a new test. Start from
the labeled defaults in [creative cadence](references/ad-intelligence/creative-cadence.md): account
structure, batch size, budget split, the decision point, and kill and scale rules. Replace each
default with the user's own account data when it exists, and say which you replaced. The matching
platform pack holds its account setup:
[Meta acquisition](references/ad-intelligence/meta-cold-traffic.md),
[Meta retargeting](references/ad-intelligence/meta-retargeting.md),
[Facebook and Instagram feeds](references/platform-intelligence/facebook.md),
[Reels and Stories](references/platform-intelligence/reels.md),
[Google Ads](references/ad-intelligence/google-ads.md),
[Apple Ads](references/ad-intelligence/apple-search-ads.md),
[LinkedIn Ads](references/ad-intelligence/linkedin-ads.md), or
[TikTok Ads](references/ad-intelligence/tiktok-ads.md).

Choose the optimization event that arrives in time for the platform to learn from it. A faster event
(trial start, lead) is a proxy: model the paid outcome from the user's real conversion rate. Format
choices, creator production, and pre-landers are in
[message transmutation](references/message-transmutation.md).

For a full campaign package, work in this order: the [strategist](agents/strategist.md) sets the
concepts, event, structure, budget, and decision rules; write the ads as above; the
[format checker](agents/format-checker.md) counts each component against the platform facts; then
check that the budget arithmetic, decision rules, and event match the plan. The
[walkthrough](references/examples/write-ad-walkthrough.md) shows a full test plan. Deliver the ads,
creative direction, destination requirements, test plan, and the open checks.

This command plans the test. Real results belong to `results`; never present planned numbers as
observed ones.

## Before launch

For claim, permission, and platform review before launch, use the
[policy floor](references/policy-floor.md) and [format spec](references/format-spec.md). Score with
the [rubric](references/rubric.md) only when the user wants a verdict.

Never launch, publish, spend, upload an audience or asset, or change a live account without explicit
approval for that exact action. A format pass or a rubric score is an editorial step; it does not
authorize launch or spend. When `campaign` calls this method, keep its offer, budget authority, and
campaign ID. For Vietnamese copy, the public `vietnamese` skill may be named as an optional helper
when installed; no polish pass may change prices, terms, claims, or the destination URL.
